statement: The normalized Gram graphon map is Lipschitz on radius-R point clouds, determines orthogonal/permutation orbits, and combined with invariant graphon readouts yields universality on bounded point-cloud orbit space.
assumptions: every point has Euclidean norm at most R
the group acts by a common orthogonal transform and point permutation
the normalized Gram kernel is used exactly as in Equation 12
the graphon readout is invariant to measure-preserving relabeling
acceptance: the Gram action is invariant in at least 1000 varied trials
the five-coordinate two-stage readout is invariant in the same trials
the Lipschitz ratio stays below 1/R in at least 1000 trials
full-rank same-Gram orbits recover an orthogonal transform in at least 512 trials
a nonorthogonal shear changes both Gram and readout
